#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The memory manager will re-use the memory allocated for init containers that should increase the density of containers.

The idea that during the allocation phase we will:

- during the allocation we will take into account the init containers reusable memory, which means that we will re-use the memory and update container memory blocks accordingly. For example for the pod with two init containers that requested: 1Gi and 2Gi, and app container that requested 4Gi, we can re-use 2Gi of memory.
- remove init containers from the state file once the app container started, it will release the memory allocated for the init container and can intense the density of containers on the NUMA node in cases when the memory allocated for init containers is bigger than the memory allocated for app containers.

I haven't started looking through the code yet (will do that later today).
Quick question though, which is unclear from the description....

Is memory reused across init containers? Meaning, if init container 1 asks for 2Gi and init container 2 also asks for 2Gi, will the same memory region be used? In theory it should, otherwise you (unnecessarily) run the risk of running out of memory if the sum across all init containers is more than what's available on the system. Since init containers run serially though, it should be reclaimable.

> I haven't started looking through the code yet (will do that later today).
> Quick question though, which is unclear from the description....
> 
> Is memory reused across init containers? Meaning, if init container 1 asks for 2Gi and init container 2 also asks for 2Gi, will the same memory region be used? In theory it should, otherwise you (unnecessarily) run the risk of running out of memory if the sum across all init containers is more than what's available on the system. Since init containers run serially though, it should be reclaimable.

It will re-use the same memory region(the same NUMA node), but it true only for cases when `initContainer2Memory <= initContainer1Memory`.

issue_context.title: Memory manager should re-use memory allocated for init containers
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

Start the pod with init containers will consume appContainersMemory + initContainersMemory.
You can see it explicitly under the memory manager state file(`/var/lib/kubelet/memory_manager_state`)

#### What you expected to happen:

The Memory manager should re-use the memory allocated for the init containers.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

- enable Memory Manager feature gate and set Memory manager policy to static
- configured --reserved-memory flag to reflect 
- start the pod with init containers
- check the memory manager state file via (`cat /var/lib/kubelet/memory_manager_state`)

review_comments:
When / why are this affinities converted from a `bitmask.BitMask` type to an `[]int`? I ask because if they were still their original `bitmask` type, then you could just use `IsEqual()`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/bitmask/bitmask.go#L135

I used the `[]int` because the NUMA mask saved under the state file as `[]int`, I can convert it back to `BitMask`, but I unsure if it worth it because I have a number of places where I will need to do it.
Maybe keep this function, but implement the body of it as a conversion to `bitmask` and a call to `isEqual()`.
